question: Recovery of a deformed lead slug with helical rifling marks at post-mortem conclusively establishes that the wound was inflicted by a licensed commercial firearm rather than a country-made weapon.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Rifling marks indicate a rifled barrel, but both licensed commercial firearms and some country-made weapons have rifled barrels. Establishing the specific weapon requires firearms identification by a ballistics expert comparing striations against the recovered projectile.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Rifling marks establish that a rifled barrel was used, but country-made (kattha) firearms can also have rifled barrels. Establishing the exact weapon requires ballistic matching against the suspect firearm; rifling marks alone cannot exclude country-made weapons.
